strengths: The sequence is clear: compare availability, select a candidate, review the choice, then confirm a local result. All supplied schedule facts are represented accurately.
Thursday’s all-four overlap is evident through counts, explicit availability labels, summary copy and visual emphasis; understanding does not depend on color.
Desktop cards align for comparison. Mobile stacks candidates and groups participants into readable two-column blocks, with the first complete candidate near the opening.

Selected and confirmed captures establish distinct visible states. Selection adds text and a checkmark; confirmation explicitly states that the choice exists only on this page and no invitations were sent.

Bold typography, restrained greens, consistent rules and clear button hierarchy form a coherent interface. The full page, including the closing section and footer, remains visually consistent without introducing unsupported claims.
limits: Static captures do not verify pointer, keyboard or touch operation, focus handling, screen-reader announcements, or actual persistence.
Only the supplied widths and Thursday’s selected and confirmed states were inspected; other candidate results, intermediate widths and zoom remain unverified.
Contrast was not numerically measured. No external design reference was supplied.
